What will SMS build next, and in what order?

Long image

A

Answer

SMS already watches Qanty and alerts Telegram. The next cycle closes four P0 gaps, then builds the dashboard, in five PRs after the open profiles PR (#23).

  1. The booker only fills the form. It does not choose a slot, submit, or confirm the appointment.
  2. Any Telegram chat can subscribe and start a booking with the owner's profiles.
  3. The scheduler does not save alerts or appointments in Postgres, so history is lost on restart.
  4. Docker only runs the dashboard. Postgres, the API, and the scheduler are missing for 24/7 operation.

Applies toSMScurrent state and five-PR planNovember 2026

1

What is SMS, in plain terms?

SMS is a personal assistant for medicine-dispensing appointments. It watches the Qanty portal, applies three business rules, and sends a Telegram alert with one button per profile. A human taps a button, and a headless browser fills the booking form.

TermMeaning
QantyThe portal where appointments are checked and booked.
SlotA date and time that may be available.
ProfileA person the system can book for.
SchedulerThe always-running process that polls Qanty and sends alerts.
BookerThe Playwright component that fills the booking form.
AllowlistThe list of Telegram chats allowed to use the bot.
tRPCThe typed function call between the dashboard and the API. Explained in the next panel.
PostgresThe database for profiles and appointments.
P0A blocker that must be fixed before production.

Current limit

The booker only fills the form. It does not select a slot, submit, or confirm. The system is not ready for production.

2

What is tRPC, in one minute?

tRPC is a typed function call between the dashboard and the API. The dashboard imports the router's TypeScript type, so a wrong input or output fails at compile time, not in production.

Think of the router as a restaurant menu: the kitchen defines the dishes, the menu lists them, and the waiter can only order what is on the menu.

Diagram structure
  • Dashboard web
  • API server api
  • profilesRouter router
  • Postgres db
  • web → api · profiles.list.query()
  • api → router · check session + input
  • router → db · SELECT profiles
  • db → router · rows
  • router → api · Profile[]
  • api → web · typed JSON
TermMeaning
RouterA group of procedures. appRouter combines profiles, appointments, and privateData.
ProcedureOne callable function, such as profiles.list or profiles.create.
QueryA read procedure, such as list.
MutationA write procedure, such as create, update, or delete.
ContextPer-request data: session and db.
MiddlewareCode that runs before a procedure. protectedProcedure rejects requests without a session.

The API server mounts the router at /trpc in apps/server/src/index.ts. The dashboard calls it with useTRPC() in apps/web/src/app/dashboard/dashboard.tsx.

3

How is the system built today?

  • The scheduler is the always-running process.
  • The dashboard is a separate Next.js app.
  • The tRPC API is the only path from the dashboard to Postgres.
  • The scheduler includes the poller, the rules engine, the session harvester, and the Playwright booker.

Diagram structure
  • Dashboard web
  • API (tRPC) api
  • Postgres db
  • Scheduler scheduler
  • Qanty portal qanty
  • Telegram bot bot
  • web → api · tRPC
  • api → db · Drizzle
  • scheduler → db · data
  • scheduler → qanty · poll and book
  • scheduler → bot · alerts
  • bot → scheduler · callback

Design note

The original Excalidraw sketch proposed a webhook and a Scheduler MCP. The current code uses Telegram long polling and direct Playwright. This plan does not add MCP. It closes the P0 gaps in the current design.

4

What happens today when a slot appears?

Today the success message arrives before an appointment exists. The real-booking PR adds submit, saves the appointment in Postgres, and moves confirmation to the end.

Diagram structure

  • Alert Telegram alert
  • User taps Book tap
  • Fill form fill
  • Select and submit submit
  • Save appointment save
  • Confirm to user confirm
  • alert → tap · button
  • fill → submit · next PR
  • poll → alert · slot
  • save → confirm · booked
  • submit → save · confirmation
  • tap → fill · callback
5

What is missing, and why does it matter?

These gaps block production. P0 means fix before production, P1 means fix soon, and P2 means product work.

PriorityGapEvidenceEffect
P0 · bookingBooking is not completedplaywrightBooker.ts fills the form and returns success: true without submittingThe user thinks they have an appointment when they do not
P0 · botBot has no allowlisttelegramBot.ts adds any chat that sends /startAnyone can see profiles and start a booking
P0 · dataNo persistenceThe scheduler does not write to the appointment tableHistory and deduplication are lost on restart
P0 · deployIncomplete deploymentdocker-compose.yml only defines webCannot run 24/7 with Postgres and the scheduler
P1 · timezoneHost timezonetodayLocalString uses local timeIn UTC, valid alerts are missed for about 5 hours
P1 · stateIn-memory stateDedup, circuit breaker, and sessions live in RAMRestart re-notifies and resets the cooldown
P1 · logsNo observabilityOnly console.logA silent failure goes unnoticed
P2 · UIDashboard scaffold21 lines, only privateDataNo CRUD or history in the UI

Before production

The current system does not complete real bookings. Do not use it in production until the real-booking PR is closed.

6

In what order will we build it?

The order protects the flow: close security and real booking first, then deploy, and only then build the UI on trusted data. The first step is the open profiles PR (#23). If it is already merged, start at Secure the bot.

Diagram structure
  • Profiles in DB merge
  • Secure the bot secure
  • Real booking booking
  • Real deployment deploy
  • Dashboard dashboard
  • Hardening harden
  • booking → deploy
  • dashboard → harden
  • deploy → dashboard
  • merge → booking · profiles in DB
  • secure → booking
